title: Anti-discrimination laws

draft.title: Anti-discrimination laws
card: Discrimination is treating a person unfairly because of a group they belong to, such as their race or sex. Before these laws, much of it was not against the law in Australia.
made it unlawful to treat people unfairly because of their race, colour, or national or ethnic origin. The Commonwealth Parliament passed it.
made it unlawful to treat people unfairly because of their sex, or because they are married or pregnant. It applies in areas such as work and education.
A person who faces unlawful discrimination can make a complaint. The laws turned a call for fair treatment into a legal right.
draft.remember: Two federal Acts, in 1975 and 1984, made unfair treatment because of race or sex unlawful.

a.q: What did the Sex Discrimination Act of 1984 do?
opts: Made unfair treatment because of sex unlawful
Set the same wage for all jobs of equal value
Allowed married women to keep public service jobs
Gave every person the rights in a UN declaration
a.why: The Act made unfair treatment because of sex against the law. Equal pay and the marriage bar are separate changes that dealt with specific rules, not a general ban on discrimination.
a.clue: Think about what the word discrimination means in the Act's title.

b.q: In 1990, a company in Perth refuses to hire Aisha because of her ethnic origin. Which law did this treatment break?
opts: The Racial Discrimination Act of 1975
The Sex Discrimination Act of 1984
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
The Commonwealth Constitution of 1901
b.why: Refusing a job because of ethnic origin is racial discrimination, which the 1975 Act made unlawful. The 1984 Act covers sex, so it does not fit this case.
b.clue: Match the reason for the treatment to the Act that covers it.

a.best: Made unfair treatment because of sex unlawful

problems.detail: The Act's name in the question ('Sex Discrimination') nearly states the answer, and the clue tells students to read the title. A student can match 'sex' and 'discrimination' to the right option without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: Anti-discrimination laws
card: Discrimination is treating a person unfairly because of a group they belong to, such as their race or sex. Before these laws, much of it was not against the law in Australia.
made it unlawful to treat people unfairly because of their race, colour, or national or ethnic origin. It covers areas of public life such as work, housing and services.
made it unlawful to treat people unfairly because of their sex, or because they are married or pregnant. It applies in areas such as work and education.
The Commonwealth Parliament passed both Acts. A person who faces unlawful discrimination can make a complaint, so a call for fair treatment became a legal right.
proposal.remember: Two federal Acts, in 1975 and 1984, made unfair treatment because of race or sex unlawful.

a.q: Before 1975, an Australian landlord could legally refuse a tenant because of their colour. What did the 1975 law change?
opts: Refusing a tenant for their colour became unlawful
Refusing a tenant became unlawful for any reason
Only unfair treatment at work became unlawful
Refusing a tenant for their sex became unlawful
a.why: The 1975 Act made unfair treatment because of race or colour unlawful, including in housing. It did not ban every refusal, only those based on grounds such as race, and sex was covered later by the 1984 Act.
a.clue: Think about which ground for unfair treatment the 1975 law covered.

b.q: In 1990, a company in Perth refuses to hire Aisha because of her ethnic origin. Which law did this treatment break?
opts: The Racial Discrimination Act of 1975
The Sex Discrimination Act of 1984
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
The Commonwealth Constitution of 1901
b.why: Refusing a job because of ethnic origin is racial discrimination, which the 1975 Act made unlawful. The 1984 Act covers sex, so it does not fit this case.
b.clue: Match the reason for the treatment to the Act that covers it.
